_comment: WHY A COMMITTED CASE (ADR 0008): /flow:auto Steps 4 and 6 read this guard's verdict
before commit and nothing downstream re-derives that no edit leaked into main.
The cases force the guard's THIRD states - could-not-look and nothing-to-look-at - which
were byte-identical to a clean pass before #1014. run-case.sh builds a real repository
and linked worktree per run; nothing is committed as a .git directory.

cases.name: bad-git-cannot-answer
cases.why: A git that cannot resolve its own git dir. The gate could not look, and before #1014 that fell into the same silent `exit 0` as a clean pass; it must now report `unknown` (exit 4).
cases.expected_output: FLOW_WORKTREE_GUARD_CONTROL: finding - gate exit 4: FLOW_WORKTREE_GUARD: unknown - git could not resolve this checkout's git dir or common dir

cases.name: bad-main-checkout
cases.why: The main checkout itself - the current-branch lane. There is no separate tree to leak into, which is `not-applicable` (exit 5), a different fact from a clean look; before #1014 it was the same silent `exit 0`.
cases.expected_output: FLOW_WORKTREE_GUARD_CONTROL: finding - gate exit 5: FLOW_WORKTREE_GUARD: not-applicable - this is the main checkout, with no separate tree to leak into

cases.name: good-clean-linked-worktree
cases.why: A linked worktree whose main tree is clean: the gate looked and found no leak, `no-leak` exit 0. Treating every run as suspect would falsely flag this.

anchors.why: The guard as it stood on main at 40f771c, byte for byte: every could-not-look and nothing-to-look-at path ended in a silent `exit 0`. It MISSES both BAD cases and AGREES with the real gate on the GOOD one - so the distinction the control pins is exactly the one #1014 added.
